changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: For payments leaders and finance buyers: Your approvals, market by market: where you have "money left on the table", why, and what we'd fix. Lead with the customer's own approval rates by country. Use "approvals", not "authorization". Keep the average uplift and the feature names out of the headline.
changes.why: The rep pitched the average uplift and Stefan dismissed it ("that's an average. What's mine?", "I can't take an average to my CFO"), and he describes the problem as approvals and "Money left on the table."

changes.current_line: Support plans with tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage.
changes.change: For accounts with international volume: A named person at Stripe reviews your approvals by market with you every month.
changes.why: Stefan asked who at Stripe looks at his numbers every month and the rep had no name, the account had gone about nine or ten months without a review, and he said "I heard from Stripe when I said I was leaving."

changes.change: For international accounts weighing local acquiring: An analysis of your own traffic, reported by country, card type and issuer, with the reasons behind each decline pattern, delivered within days. Confirm the turnaround with the payments performance team before using the timing claim.
changes.why: Adyen won on method with a country-level test on his own traffic, and our market-by-market analysis, which he called the most useful thing we'd sent, arrived three weeks after he asked, when the test was already finished.
